Etant donné le corpus qui grossit au cours du temps,
J'ai besoin d'un benchmark qui permet de normaliser
le nombre de nouvelles par jour.

```{r}

#english reading system
Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "English")

news_data$datetime <- as.Date(format(as.Date(news_data$date, "%b %d, %Y"), "%Y-%m-%d"))

news_data$datetime <- ifelse( is.na(news_data$datetime), as.Date(format(as.Date(news_data$date, "%d %b %Y"), "%Y-%m-%d")), news_data$datetime)

news_data <- news_data %>% 
  mutate(datetime = as.Date(datetime)) %>% 
  arrange(datetime)

# Define keywords as a list
gas_keywords <- c("gas", "Gazprom", "LNG")
# Create a regular expression pattern from the list
gas_pattern <- paste(gas_keywords, collapse = "|")
# Filter rows in news_data based on the title containing any keyword
filtered_news <- news_data[grepl(gas_pattern, news_data$title, ignore.case = TRUE), ]

#  Look for Typical Sentence Structures
# Affirmative sentences often follow a [subject-verb-object (SVO)] structure, like "The cat sits on the mat."

# Define the keywords you want to exclude
exclude_keywords <- c( "edible",  "food", "biofuel", "continue", "still",
                       "\\?", "station", "gasoline", "diesel")
# ? most often are title of opinion pieces
#that don't bring new informations

# Create a single pattern from the keywords
exclude_pattern <- paste(exclude_keywords, collapse = "|")
# Filter out rows where 'title' contains any of the exclude keywords
filtered_news <- filtered_news[!grepl(exclude_pattern, filtered_news$title, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
# Expression régulière pour détecter un verbe conjugué à la voix active
verbe_actif_regex <- "\\b(\\w+ed|\\w+s|\\w+ing)\\b"

View(filtered_news %>% 
  mutate(active = grepl(verbe_actif_regex, title)) %>% 
    select(datetime, title, active))

filtered_news_distinct <- filtered_news %>% 
  select(-event_type) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  arrange(desc(datetime))

filtered_news_active <- filtered_news_distinct %>% 
  mutate(active = grepl(verbe_actif_regex, title)) %>% 
  filter(active==TRUE)


# news_data <- news_data %>% 
#   select(-datetime)

demand_keywords <- c("demand ", "inventory", "stocks")
demand_pattern <- paste(demand_keywords, collapse = "|")
demand_filtered_news  <- filtered_news_distinct[grepl(demand_pattern, filtered_news_distinct$title, ignore.case = TRUE), ]%>% 
  mutate(event_type = "demand")

supply_keywords <- c("supply", "production", "Iraq","Iran", "Russia", "Ukraine","Israel", "Libya", "crisis", "attack", "Qatar",
                     "violence", "conflict", "war ","reserves", "refinery", "pipeline","facility", "ban", "shale")
supply_pattern <- paste(supply_keywords, collapse = "|")
supply_filtered_news <- filtered_news_distinct[grepl(supply_pattern, filtered_news_distinct$title, ignore.case = TRUE), ]%>% 
  mutate(event_type = "supply")

uncertainty_keywords <- c("uncertainty", "fear", "concern",
                          "threaten", "risk", "turmoil",
                          "tension", "worr", "turmoil",
                          "surprise", "shock")
uncertainty_pattern <- paste(uncertainty_keywords, collapse = "|")
uncertainty_filtered_news <- filtered_news_distinct[grepl(uncertainty_pattern, filtered_news_distinct$title, ignore.case = TRUE), ]%>% 
  mutate(event_type = "uncertainty")

```

Browsing the news titles, you can assess that the news titles are not very reliable.
Sometimes the connection with supply or demand is weak,
sometimes it is obviously wrong.

Thus, I filter again my news corpus by keywords


On fait de même en ayant classé les news par thème

```{r}

# Créer un dataframe avec les types d'événements
event_types <- data.frame(event_type = c("supply", "demand", "uncertainty"))

# Créer toutes les combinaisons de dates et d'événements
full_event_dates <- full_dates %>%
  crossing(event_types)

# Joindre avec les données de nouvelles
event_complete_data <- full_event_dates %>%
  left_join(event_news_count, by = c("datetime", "event_type")) %>%
  replace_na(list(news_per_day = 0))

ggplot(event_complete_data, aes(x = datetime, y = news_per_day, color = event_type)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Number of news per day",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Number of news") +
  theme_minimal()

```

On affiche les quelques jours avec le plus de nouvelles




Il faut se fixer un seuil d'identification des chocs potentiellement variable avec le temps. Une normalisation par rapport à la quantité de news disponibles.
Il peut être différent pour les supply and demand, puisqu'il semble qu'il y ait plus de nouvelles de supply que de demand.


Definir un seuil flottant
par supérieur à 3 fois la moyenne du mois
On double checke en regardant le nombre de jours d'annonce que cela permet de sélectionner.


```{r}
supply_news_count <- event_news_count %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = event_type, values_from = news_per_day) %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace_na(., 0))) %>% 
  mutate(day_type = ifelse(supply < 3*demand, "ambiguous", "supply")) %>% 
  select(supply, demand, day_type)

# Fusionner le DataFrame original avec la séquence complète de dates
complete_data <- full_dates %>%
  left_join(supply_news_count , by = "datetime") %>%
  rename(supply_news = supply, demand_news = demand) %>%
  replace_na(list(supply_news = 0, demand_news = 0))


shock_data_supply <- complete_data %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%  # Replace 'date_column' with your actual date column name
  mutate(moving_avg_news_supply = rollapply(supply_news, width = 30, FUN = mean, fill = NA),
         moving_std_news_supply = rollapply(supply_news, width = 30, FUN = sd, fill = NA),
         supply_shock= (supply_news >  moving_avg_news_supply + 1.9*moving_std_news_supply),
         moving_avg_news_demand = rollapply(demand_news, width = 30, FUN = mean, fill = NA),
         moving_std_news_demand = rollapply(demand_news, width = 30, FUN = sd, fill = NA),
         demand_shock= (demand_news >  moving_avg_news_demand + 1.9*moving_std_news_demand)
         )


info_supply <- merge(gas_data_shock, shock_data_supply, 
              by.x = "Date", by.y = "datetime" ) 

instrument_days_supply <- info_supply %>% 
  filter(supply_shock ==TRUE) %>% 
  filter(supply_news > 4) %>% 
  filter(day_type == "supply")

nrow(instrument_days_supply)
```

```{r}
shock_info_supply <- info_supply %>% 
  mutate(order = abs(shock_serie),
         ptstat = (supply_news -moving_avg_news_supply)/moving_std_news_supply ) %>% 
  arrange(desc(order)) %>% 
  slice(1:20) %>% 
  select(Date, order, supply_news, 
          ptstat, supply_shock, demand_shock, day_type)

shock_info_supply
```

```{r}
info_selected <- info_selected %>%
    mutate(instrumented_day = ifelse(binary_shock == TRUE & news_per_day > 3, "supply_shock", 0),
           instrumented_day = ifelse(Date %in% demand_news_days, "demand_shock", instrumented_day))

                                  select(time, dms_M1), by = c( "time"))

supply_shock_serie <- info_selected %>% 
  filter(instrumented_day=="supply_shock") %>% 
  mutate(month = month(Date), year= year(Date))%>%
  group_by(month, year) %>%

  arrange(Date)

  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date)) %>% 
  arrange(Date)
```

```{r}

shock_series_all <- full_join(supply_shock_serie ,events_data_serie%>% select(-Date),
                              by = c("month", 'year')) %>% 
  filter(as.numeric(year)> 2014)
# Convert "Month_Year" to Date format (assume 1st day of the month)
shock_series_all$Date <- as.Date(paste0(shock_series_all$year, "-",shock_series_all$month,  "-15"))


# Get the min and max dates
min_date <- min(shock_series_all$Date)
max_date <- max(shock_series_all$Date)

# Create a sequence of full months between min and max dates
months_seq <- seq(min_date, max_date, by = "month")

# Calculate the middle of each month (e.g., 15th day)
middle_dates <- as.Date(paste0(format(months_seq, "%Y-%m-15")))


shock_series_all <- left_join(tibble(Date = middle_dates), shock_series_all,  by = "Date")

# Remplir les NA avec 0
shock_series_all[is.na(shock_series_all)] <- 0

shock_series_all
  
```
